architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Define delta as the measured 120-130 C viscosity-level change relative to the unmodified reactive-core reference. Accept exactly one formulation-level hypothesis if delta lies within 3.40 percentage points of its preregistered prediction: H-LEVEL-DILUTE at -42.76%, H-LEVEL-ASSOC at 17.24%, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC at -72.76%. Report the directly measured 120 and 130 C viscosity levels and E_eta with the accepted classification.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The processing-window viscosity level is directly measured within the selected resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry, so that level observable is chemistry-supported by the sweep. The observable does not depend on transferring a rheological regularity from the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family. E_eta is a fitted rheological descriptor from the candidate's own sweep, not evidence of molecular mechanism. Shared-shape transfer to this modified chemistry remains unvalidated; the binding audit correctly permits M-SWEEP and excludes M-ANCHOR.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if delta differs from -42.76% by more than 3.40 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if delta is at or below -42.76%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if delta is at or above -42.76%. If delta is not within 3.40 percentage points of exactly one prediction, the level hypotheses are non-discriminated rather than accepted. These criteria test formulation-level rheological predictions only and do not establish molecular association or plasticization mechanisms.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT to quantify between-preparation realization-state spread using at least three independent preparations and the 80-130 C sweep protocol, then reassess the candidate-minus-reference level change with a replicate-based uncertainty interval.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C, with viscosity measured across 80-130 C in 10 C increments, together with the apparent rheological temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 combines 15% acrylic-like modifier with 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, both within the supplied evidence-supported region, while retaining the highest deterministic value among admissible cards. M-SWEEP directly measures the 120-130 C processing-window level and verifies the candidate's own temperature response rather than reconstructing it from an inadmissible transferred shape. The card is therefore scientifically defensible as a prospective formulation-level probe and mitigation experiment, provided the stated realization-state limitation is retained.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-SWEEP because it is admissible, directly measures the decision quantity in the modified chemistry, and is the smallest-acrylic member of the deterministic top tie. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: the nominal 3.40% criteria are not operationally defensible from one uncontrolled preparation given the observed realization spread, and the result must not be used to claim individual modifier causality, thermal-hold stability, or molecular mechanism.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The candidate is in an externally supported dual-axis region, but the combined 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100 intervention cannot identify individual-axis effects or interaction effects.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the directly measured 80-130 C level range. High remains for any claim that the unmodified family's shared thermal-response shape transfers to this resin-modified chemistry; that transfer is not assumed.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The catalogued M-SWEEP discrimination residual is 3.40%, but this is not a demonstrated uncertainty for a candidate-minus-reference comparison; instrument and regression uncertainty must be reported from the sweep.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High. The local E2 data show matched-temperature realization ratios of 2.80-3.57, while the selected card specifies one preparation and does not control process state. This can exceed the nominal 3.40% discrimination threshold.

action_requests.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported rheology regularities must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, reactive-core anchor, modifier axes, and historical boundary needed to define a candidate experiment that separates the registered level hypotheses.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original local reactive-polyurethane hot-melt family represented by E1-E3 and the E2 reactive-core anchor. A candidate containing acrylic-like or tackifier-like modifiers cannot be assumed to remain inside the validated chemistry support until the audited chemistry boundary is loaded; therefore the intended experiment should use a direct temperature sweep rather than rely on one-point state calibration.
planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled realized viscosity level at the processing temperature, creating a risk that a nominally selected formulation misses the processing-viscosity window.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: E2 temperature-sweep realizations show very large matched-temperature spread: max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 and sample CV values of 0.46-0.58 across 80-130 C. Thus a nominal viscosity level is not yet a reliably controlled material property.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local hold data contain only one original run for E1 and one for E5, each with four time points at 120 C. Although they show markedly different SI_15_60 values of 0.095 and 0.515, respectively, there are no repeat trajectories or modified-candidate hold profiles, so the time-dependent failure behavior is least resolved.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate viscosity directly from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample, including direct measurements at 120 and 130 C.
Use sufficient independent preparations or repeats to distinguish the candidate level from the observed realization spread and report the repeatability distribution rather than only a nominal value.
Compare the measured matched-temperature level with the preregistered inert-dilution, acrylic-association, and plasticization predictions using the stated measurement-resolution thresholds.
Fit and report the apparent temperature-response descriptor from ln(eta) versus 1/T without extrapolating beyond the measured temperature range.
If thermal stability is part of the decision, add at least two independent 120 C holds with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes so the isothermal trajectory is directly resolved.
planner.scientific_question: For a modified reactive-core candidate, does the realized viscosity level follow inert dilution alone, rise above dilution as predicted by acrylic-like association, or fall below dilution as predicted by plasticizing modifiers, and does its directly measured 80-130 C temperature response remain compatible with the local shared response?

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported rheology regularities must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, reactive-core anchor, modifier axes, and historical boundary needed to define a candidate experiment that separates the registered level hypotheses.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate is resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry, outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. The binding audit therefore excludes M-ANCHOR but permits M-SWEEP because the sweep directly measures the candidate response and verifies rather than assumes thermal-shape transfer. The viscosity level is consequently directly interpretable for this candidate; E_eta remains a fitted rheological descriptor.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the measured 120-130 C level change relative to the unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one prediction, the corresponding hypothesis is accepted for S1C41: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. The directly measured processing-window level and the candidate temperature response are then reported with that hypothesis.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured change is at or below the inert-dilution prediction of -42.76%; H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%; and H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured change differs from -42.76% by more than 3.40%.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: If the result does not fall within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction, the outcome is non-discriminating at the stated measurement resolution. No level hypothesis is accepted; process-state variability, prediction inadequacy, or overlap with the resolution limit would require follow-up measurement rather than model-based adjudication.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the 120-130 C processing-window level, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is deterministically tied, but uses a higher acrylic loading than S1C41 and therefore imposes a larger justified departure from the characterized local chemistry without improving discrimination.
It is deterministically tied, but uses a higher 20% acrylic loading, increasing modifier burden without improving direct observability or hypothesis separation.
It is deterministically tied, but uses 22.5% acrylic, a larger intervention than necessary for the same three-hypothesis discrimination.
It is deterministically tied, but uses the maximum 25% acrylic loading and thus the greatest departure from the characterized reactive core among the tied cards.

proposer.reasoning: M-SWEEP is the highest-VOI admissible measurement plan and directly resolves the processing-window level while testing all three registered level hypotheses. S1C41 lies within the externally supported intervention regions, uses 15% acrylic and 5% tackifier, and avoids relying on an unverified shared-shape reconstruction. The direct 80-130 C sweep also establishes whether the candidate's thermal response remains compatible with the local rheological regularity.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and are scientifically tied in the deterministic layer. S1C41 uses the smallest acrylic loading in the supported 15-25% region while retaining the repeatedly supported approximately 5% minor-tackifier level, thereby minimizing modifier burden and departure from the characterized reactive core without reducing hypothesis discrimination or direct shape verification.

residual_decision_risk: Preparation and realization-state variability may exceed the nominal 3.40% discrimination threshold.
A single combined acrylic-plus-tackifier intervention cannot attribute an observed level shift to one modifier axis, their interaction, or nonideality.
M-SWEEP does not resolve thermal-hold drift or the separately registered stability hypotheses.
The apparent E_eta descriptor remains conditional on the ln(eta) versus 1/T regression model.
Shared-shape transfer to the resin-modified chemistry must not be assumed; only the directly measured candidate curve is chemistry-supported.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is that the stated 3.40% M-SWEEP threshold is not defensible with one uncontrolled preparation in a system showing 2.80-3.57x matched-temperature realization spread. This does not change the admissible experiment card: a direct 80-130 C sweep remains the appropriate measurement for the modified chemistry. It does change how its result may be interpreted: without independent S1C41 preparations, matched unmodified-core references, and a preregistered replicate-based uncertainty interval, the result should not be treated as defensible acceptance or falsification of the level hypotheses at the stated threshold. The tie does not require switching to another tied card; S1C41 is scientifically preferred because it uses the smallest acrylic loading in the supported dual-axis region while retaining the supported approximately 5% tackifier level. Attribution of individual modifier effects remains unavailable from this combined intervention.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set. The top set remains unchanged across all 29 re-weightings, with top_experiment_set_stability of 1.0, intervention-family and measurement-plan stability of 1.0, and no recommendation_flip_boundary for any weight term within the 0.5-1.5 sweep. No defensible tested reweighting changes the decision. The small base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower of 0.002292 indicates limited separation from lower-ranked cards, but not a weight-induced flip in this sweep.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary processing-window viscosity level stays inside the support of the selected measurement because M-SWEEP directly measures S1C41 from 80 to 130 C. It does not stay inside the prior support for shared-shape transfer: the prior shape was measured only for unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI, and S1C41 is resin-modified AC1920/TK100. Direct temperature-sweep verification, as selected, is required before any shared-shape compatibility claim.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The numerical predictions are separated by much more than the nominal 3.40% M-SWEEP resolution, but the protocol has min_repeats = 1 and does not control process state. Because the local data show very large matched-temperature realization spread, the experiment cannot establish that a 3.40% departure from -42.76% is larger than measurement and preparation variability. Replicate-based uncertainty and a matched reference measurement are required before the acceptance and falsification boundaries are operationally credible.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could support only a static level classification for S1C41, not a claim about hot-hold stability, modifier functionality, or a preferred stability region.
objections.objection: The three registered level predictions for S1C41 are numerically separated: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, versus the M-SWEEP threshold of 3.40%. Thus the level hypotheses are separable in principle. However, the experiment does not separate the separately registered stability hypotheses H1-H3 or the thermal-hold behavior; M-SWEEP has no time sampling and the hypothesis registry explicitly limits these level hypotheses to formulation-level viscosity statements.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result above or below dilution could be reported as support for an acrylic-association or plasticization explanation without the design establishing which axis caused it.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: 15% AC1920 acrylic-like modifier and 5% TK100 minor tackifier-like modifier, leaving a reactive mass fraction of 0.80. Although the aggregate predictions are distinct, this composition cannot identify whether any departure from the -42.76% inert-dilution prediction is caused by acrylic association, tackifier plasticization, their interaction, or simple composition-specific nonideality. The proposer claims separation of H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, but the experiment cannot attribute the observed effect to either modifier mechanism independently.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct candidate curve may be reliable while the reported relative change and assignment to one registered prediction remain confounded with reference-batch and realization-state differences.
objections.objection: The candidate viscosity at 120 and 130 C is directly measured by M-SWEEP, so the within-candidate processing-window level is interpretable. However, the primary discrimination quantity is the percentage change 'against the unmodified reactive core' and the protocol specifies only one fresh S1C41 preparation, with no matched contemporaneous unmodified-core preparation or prespecified uncertainty calculation for that differential. The 3.40% threshold is the residual of a shared-shape-plus-intercept fit, not an demonstrated resolution for a candidate-minus-reference comparison across independent preparations.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The protocol may label ordinary realization-state variation as falsification or acceptance, so the stated 3.40% criterion is not practically attainable as a defensible hypothesis test.
objections.objection: The M-SWEEP card specifies min_repeats = 1 and controls_process_state = false, while the audited E2 data show 2.80-3.57x matched-temperature realization spread and the card assigns process_state_risk = 0.75. A single 80-130 C sweep cannot demonstrate that a departure of more than 3.40% from the -42.76% dilution prediction exceeds preparation and realization variability. The inequality criteria for H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC likewise use the exact dilution boundary without a replicate-based uncertainty margin.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No additional chemistry-domain claim is supported beyond the directly swept S1C41 temperature response; the experiment cannot assume unmodified shared-shape transfer before the sweep.
objections.objection: The selected M-SWEEP is appropriate for the domain boundary: S1C41 is resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry, outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family, and the audit marks M-ANCHOR inadmissible but M-SWEEP admissible. The viscosity level is measured directly across 80-130 C rather than reconstructed from the unmodified shared shape. The fitted E_eta descriptor still inherits the ln(eta) versus 1/T regression model, but this does not undermine direct level measurement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological level shift could be incorrectly presented as proof of molecular association, plasticization, or modifier-specific interaction.
objections.objection: The experiment can test the registered formulation-level viscosity statements, but neither the M-SWEEP protocol nor the primary observable can establish the molecular mechanism stated informally by labels such as 'association' or 'plasticization.' The payload's hypothesis registry correctly says these are formulation-level predictions rather than molecular-mechanism claims; any mechanistic interpretation beyond that boundary would exceed the measurement.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct 80-130 C sweep but run at least two or three independent S1C41 preparations and matched unmodified-core reference preparations under the same recorded process history, then preregister a replicate-based uncertainty interval for the candidate-minus-reference level change. Add single-axis acrylic-only and tackifier-only controls if attribution between H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is intended.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The stated 3.40% falsification threshold is not defensible with M-SWEEP as specified: S1C41 receives only one preparation, process state is uncontrolled, and the audited local realization spread is 2.80-3.57x. The protocol therefore cannot distinguish a prediction error of 3.40% from ordinary preparation-state variation.

tool_trace.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported rheology regularities must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above that same prediction. H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured level change departs from -38.18% by more than the 3.40% resolution of this plan.

measurement_plan.name: 80-130 C temperature sweep
measurement_plan.primary_observable: directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 27.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The 80-130 C sweep is the direct verification measurement that establishes the thermal-response shape for a chemistry-shifted candidate.
